findings.description: Two concurrent `pup intent new` calls with different titles can both take the same NNNN. The `wx` flag only catches a clash on the exact same file name, so both files are written, and from then on `show` and `accept` refuse that id.
findings.body:
`createIntent` picks the next id from a single directory listing, then creates the file exclusively under a name that **includes the slug**:

```ts
const next = Math.max(0, ...intentFiles(dir).map((file) => Number(file.id))) + 1;
...
const path = join(dir, `${id}-${slug(clean)}.md`);
...
writeFileSync(path, intentTemplate(id, clean), { flag: 'wx' });
```

`wx` (`O_EXCL`) only fails when the *same file name* exists. If two writers list the directory before either writes (ADR 0126 lets the operator, the conductor and any session run `new` against the same main-checkout `docs/intent/`), and their titles differ, one writes `0005-alpha.md`, the other `0005-beta.md`, and both succeed. The `EEXIST` branch ("appeared while creating it; run it again"), which exists for exactly this race, never fires.

Afterwards `intentPath` refuses id 0005 for both `show` and `accept` (`Intent 0005 has 2 files ...; keep one`), `list` shows two entries with the same id, and recovery needs a rename *plus* an edit of the `# NNNN.` title line, since `loadIntent` rejects a title id that doesn't match the file name. ADR 0126 does not accept this race.

Possible fixes: after the `wx` write, re-list and, if another file shares the id, unlink yours and retry with the next id; or reserve the id itself exclusively (an id-only name) before writing the slugged file.

findings.description: visibleLines only hides HTML comments that start a line, so a comment opened after a tag inside an HTML block (`<div><!--`) hides a `- Status: accepted` line on GitHub but not from pup. A `* Status: draft` bullet then shows draft on GitHub while pup parses accepted, which breaks ADR 0126's 'never a forged status' guarantee.
A UTF-8 BOM is not removed, so a hand-edited intent saved with one shows as `unreadable` ("does not open with `# NNNN. <title>`").

The fence regexes were copied from `brief.service.ts`, but the level-2 heading parser was rewritten and behaves differently: `SECTION_HEADING = /^ {0,3}## (.*)$/` rejects a tab after `##` and keeps a closing `#` run that brief's `headingTitle` strips, so `## What I must understand after review ##` is never the understanding section here.

`intentDir(repoPath, { create = false } = {})` always returns `string | undefined`, even though `create: true` never returns undefined, which forces `as string` casts at L103 and L225; an overload or a separate `ensureIntentDir` would state the contract instead.

`intent.types.ts` sits flat in `src/core/`, but `docs/conventions/general.md` puts exported types under `src/core/types/`, where all 18 sibling `*.types.ts` files live; move it to `src/core/types/intent.types.ts`.

`intent.enums.ts` and `intent.errors.ts` sit flat in `src/core/` though `general.md` puts enums in `enums/` and errors in `errors/` (flat `*.errors.ts` precedent exists and ADR 0126 discloses the placement).
`intent-service.test.ts` is colocated in `src/core/` while `testing.md` wants unit tests under `test/unit/core/` (that folder doesn't exist yet and ADR 0126 discloses the placement).

The ADR gives the file pattern as `^NNNN-[a-z0-9-]+\.md$`, but `INTENT_FILE` is `^([0-9]{4})-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\.md$`, which rejects doubled, leading or trailing hyphens; a file like `0001-a--b.md` matches the ADR but is ignored by the code.
The ADR says `createIntent`, `readIntent`, `listIntents`, `acceptIntent` and `intentTemplate` each take the repo path, but `intentTemplate(id, title)` takes none.

The ADR's *Interface for part 2*, *Layout* and *Tests* paragraphs restate export names, file placement and per-case test counts ("six", "eleven", "eight ways") that rot on any refactor; trim them to the WHY.
The `pup intent` entry runs ~15 lines repeating ADR 0126's parsing and path rules where sibling entries cite the decision for mechanics, and its wrapping is ragged ("An id is" breaks early).

The comment above `intent show`'s `console.log(readIntent(...))` repeats that core strips control characters keeping newline and tab, which `Intent.text`'s JSDoc in `intent.types.ts` already states; delete it.

`pup intent accept`'s operator-only check relies on the caller's env vars and current directory, the same as brief, conductor, watch and debt close. A session that leaves its worktree and unsets PUP_SESSION_ID and PUP_CONDUCTOR passes as the operator, and any shell can set `- Status: accepted` by hand. Both are documented limits (decision 27's ceiling in ADRs 0042, 0044 and 0047; ADR 0126 'Who' and 'Part 2 must not trust a status it did not write').
